turn_text: Welcome back to the Jim Lee Show. Monthly we have checked in with our next guest, but this apparently is going to be the last time we do that, certainly with his current title. I didn't really envision I'd be saying this, but joining us now is soon to be former State Senator Andy Menar. Senator, welcome to the program. Great to have you here.
Well, as always, Jim, thank you for having

me. And a happy new year. And I got to admit, I was blind, sad. I think most people were when the news came down yesterday that you were resigning your seat in the General Assembly to join Governor J.B. Pritzker's administration. What prompted all this?

Well, it's hard to point to one thing. Certainly, I would tell you and the listeners, and more importantly, my constituents, that there are so many things that go into a decision like this. We're nearing the end of a general assembly, so this would be a good time for a transition if there ever was one. Number two, I look forward to new opportunities and serving in Governor Pritzker's administration, I think, is not just an opportunity for me, which isn't the guiding force, but will allow me to use my experience to help both his administration and ultimately the people of the state. And number three, Jim, I would tell you that I mean you know this and the listeners that have gotten to know me and watched me over the years know that when I started this my children were quite young and today Tristan I are proud parents of three two of which are teenagers and while we say our family is always first it is but there's an asterisk next to that and There's always a additional weight being an elected official and my family has never known a day otherwise. My wife and I met when I was the mayor of Bunker Hill, when I was the budget director for President Emile Jones years ago. When we were on our honeymoon, I was making calls to my colleagues on the Coopin County Board to try to earn their vote. And I felt like I owed that to my family at the end of the day, especially since two of our children now teens. So those are three things. There are others, but I would put those in the larger categories of things that brought me to this decision.

But honestly, I think the biggest thing is accountability. I'm proud of that.
